messages:
jonathan_cust: hey team — embeddings endpoint suddenly started returning vectors of length 1536 for us, our app expects 1024 and downstream indexing is breaking. started after we upgraded to the latest python sdk.

maya_support: sorry you're hitting this, jonathan. can you paste the exact request (headers + payload) or the SDK snippet? also which model id are you passing?

jonathan_cust: here's minimal repro (python):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=REDWOOD_KEY)
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="embed-latest", input=["hi","bye"]) 
print(len(resp[0]))
```
prints 1536. our index expects 1024. no errors in response.

maya_support: thanks. two quick checks: 1) can you run a curl request directly against the API to confirm it's not SDK-side munging? 2) what's the pip package version (`pip show redwood-sdk`)?

jonathan_cust: curl looks like:
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"embed-latest","input":["hi"]}' | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'
```
returns 1536 as well. pip shows redwood-sdk 0.9.3.

liwei_sdk: quick note — we shipped an embed model variant with 1536 dims behind the alias `embed-latest` for some customers testing higher-dim embeddings. appears you got routed to that variant.

maya_support: ah — that explains dim change. sorry for the surprise, jonathan. we should have auto-notified breaking changes.

jonathan_cust: ok — can we pin to the 1024 variant? our ingest pipeline is already in prod.

liwei_sdk: yes — use model `embed-1024-v2` in the request. the alias `embed-latest` may now map to 1536. you can also set the SDK to lock model version if you prefer reproducible outputs.

jonathan_cust: thanks. two follow-ups: 1) why did curl + sdk both work without error (no schema mismatch) — shouldn't API validate dimension? 2) we saw a spike in latency during retries after this change and several 504s. billing meter also shows increased token usage — is that expected?

maya_support: answers: 1) the API treats embeddings dimensions as part of model output; there is no hard validation against a client-side expected dim because the service supports multiple embedding sizes. We should add better docs/headers in responses indicating dim. 2) spikes could be from larger payloads and longer compute on the new variant — and if your client retried on a single request because of timeouts, that would increase billable units. can you share request rates and any retry/backoff settings?

jonathan_cust: we batch up to 128 inputs and send with concurrency=8. SDK default retry is 3 with exponential backoff (base 0.5s). timeouts we set to 10s per request. During the spike we saw 504s and 429s intermittently.

dave_oncall: tagging infra — big gaps: 1) new model variant may have higher latency per request. 2) batching 128 on a higher-dim model can blow up GPU memory and cause queueing. recommend reducing batch size to 64 for 1536-dim model and enabling adaptive batching.

liwei_sdk: also recommend enabling client-side validation to check embedding length on first request and fail fast (so downstream indexers don't accept wrong shapes). we'll add a warning in the SDK when using ambiguous aliases like `embed-latest`.

maya_support: next steps for you, jonathan: 1) switch to explicit model `embed-1024-v2` in prod (safe rollback). 2) temporarily reduce batch size to 32 and increase request timeout to 30s while we confirm backend SLOs. 3) share a sample of your retry logic so we can advise on idempotency and backoff to avoid double billing.

jonathan_cust: I'll change model and reduce batch size now. my retry logic is simple: on any 5xx or exception, sleep backoff * attempt and retry up to 3.

maya_support: suggest exponential backoff with jitter (capped) and only retry on idempotent calls or use dedup tokens. for embeddings, best to retry on 502/503 with jittered backoff, avoid retrying on 429 unless you examine `Retry-After`.

liwei_sdk: follow-up — we pushed a small server header change to include `X-Embedding-Dims` in responses. should be visible in a minute. that will let clients auto-detect.

support-bot: info: released redwood-sdk 0.9.4 with alias warning and model pinning helper — see release notes https://go/redwood/release/0.9.4 :rocket:

jonathan_cust: saw header, confirmed 1536 in response header. will pin to embed-1024-v2 and redeploy. thanks team.

maya_support: glad that helped. i'll file a docs task to clarify alias risks and a billing check with Finance to audit increased charges for your org during the incident. linking ticket RN-7543.

jonathan_cust: appreciate it. leaving this thread open until finance confirms no unexpected charges.

maya_support: noted. I'll update RN-7543 with ETA for the finance audit and post back here. :thumbsup:
